title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 112: The Terracotta Army of Xi'an
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 112 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Terracotta Army of Xi'an

Paragraph 1. In March 1974, during a very dry season in northern China, local farmers were digging a water well. Deep under the red earth, their shovels hit hard baked clay. They soon found broken clay heads, bronze weapons, and clay arms. Without knowing it, the farmers had discovered the giant underground tomb of Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of China, who died in 210 BCE.

Paragraph 2. Scientists later dug out a huge underground army built to guard the emperor after death. The largest underground room, called Pit 1, holds around 6,000 clay soldiers and forty wooden war carts. All these figures stand in neat lines facing east to watch for enemy attacks. Some statues are kneeling archers, while others are tall foot soldiers or high army generals.

Paragraph 3. Making thousands of statues was a smart factory job. Workers used solid clay for the legs so the statues could stand firmly, and made hollow upper bodies so they were lighter. Then artists shaped different ears, hair, and faces by hand, so no two soldiers look the same. To check quality, workers had to press their own names into the soft clay before baking.

Paragraph 4. When first built, the soldiers were not grey; they were painted in bright red, green, blue, and purple colors. Sadly, when scientists opened the wet rooms, dry outside air made the old paint peel off in minutes. The soldiers also carried real bronze swords that stayed sharp and clean after two thousand years. The secret was the tight, natural soil around them, which kept air and water out.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...local farmers were digging a water well."
Đoạn 2: "All these figures stand in neat lines facing east..."
Đoạn 3: "...workers had to press their own names into the soft clay..."
Đoạn 4: "The secret was the tight, natural soil around them..."

q5.text: The clay statues were first found by university scientists during a planned dig.

steps: Đoạn 1: Nông dân địa phương vô tình tìm thấy khi đi đào giếng nước (digging a water well).

q6.text: Every clay soldier was made with the exact same face.

steps: Đoạn 3: Nghệ nhân nặn khuôn mặt khác nhau bằng tay, không có 2 tượng nào giống hệt nhau.

q7.text: When first built, the soldiers were painted in bright colors.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...they were painted in bright red, green, blue, and purple colors."

q8.text: The central tomb of Qin Shi Huang is already open to tourists.

steps: Đoạn 1–4: Bài không đề cập lăng mộ trung tâm đã mở cho khách du lịch hay chưa.
